title: iO app won't pair with brush
shortDescription: Bluetooth handshake failing between brush and Oral-B app.
fullDescription:
iO Series 7/9/10 and Genius X brushes connect via Bluetooth. Pairing failures are usually due to the brush being fully charged but not powered on during pairing, a prior pairing cache, or location permissions disabled on the phone.

Reset pairing by holding mode for 10 seconds until the colors cycle.

fixSteps.title: Charge brush 1 hour
fixSteps.instruction: Place on charger until full.

fixSteps.title: Reset pairing
fixSteps.instruction: Hold mode button 10 seconds until LEDs cycle colors.

fixSteps.title: Enable location
fixSteps.instruction: Enable location and Bluetooth permissions for the Oral-B app.

whenToCallPro: Only for confirmed brush hardware faults.

title: App disconnects mid-brushing
shortDescription: Brush loses Bluetooth mid-session — distance, metal, or interference.
fullDescription:
The Oral-B app streams real-time motion data. A bathroom environment with metal shelving, WiFi routers, or other Bluetooth devices can break the link.

Keep the phone within 1 meter, line-of-sight, for best results.

fixSteps.title: Move phone closer
fixSteps.instruction: Keep within 1 meter of brush.

fixSteps.title: Disable battery saver
fixSteps.instruction: Allow Oral-B app to run in background.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Turn Bluetooth off/on to clear stack.

faq.q: Can it record without the app?
faq.a: iO10 stores sessions onboard; older models need the app live.

title: 30-second quadrant timer feels wrong
shortDescription: Timer calibration drifts after long power-off storage.
fullDescription:
iO brushes pulse every 30 seconds to signal quadrant change. After a deep discharge or factory reset, the timer may desync from the total 2-minute session.

Perform a full-charge reset and run one complete 2-minute session to recalibrate.

fixSteps.title: Full charge
fixSteps.instruction: Charge overnight to 100%.

fixSteps.title: Run full cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Let one complete 2-minute clean run without interruption.

fixSteps.title: Sync via app
fixSteps.instruction: Open Oral-B app to allow firmware sync.

title: Brush red LED — not accepting charge
shortDescription: Inductive charge refused due to temperature or contact issue.
fullDescription:
A red or blinking LED on the base of an iO brush indicates it is not charging correctly. Causes include a mis-seated handle, foreign object on the charger, or low-temperature protection below 5°C.

Remove and reseat the brush; allow it to warm to room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Reseat brush
fixSteps.instruction: Lift and recenter on charging post.

fixSteps.title: Warm up
fixSteps.instruction: Allow brush to reach 20°C room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Try another outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Swap outlets to rule out power issue.

whenToCallPro: Red LED persists at room temperature with new charger.

title: Blue bristles faded — replace head
shortDescription: Indicator bristles fade when head is worn after ~3 months.
fullDescription:
Oral-B brush heads have blue indicator bristles that fade to white when half-worn, signaling replacement. iO smart heads also report wear via NFC chip to the app.

Replace with genuine iO Ultimate Clean or CrossAction refills.

fixSteps.title: Pull off old head
fixSteps.instruction: Gently pull head straight off the shaft.

fixSteps.title: Click new head
fixSteps.instruction: Align and push new head until audible click.

faq.a: Standard heads fit but iO NFC features require genuine.

title: Red pressure ring illuminated continuously
shortDescription: Pressure sensor misreading — moisture or mechanical jam.
fullDescription:
The pressure sensor uses a magnetic field detector inside the handle. If the red LED stays on even without pressure, the sensor may be stuck or the handle/head alignment is off.

Remove head, wipe contacts dry, and reattach. Factory reset via mode+power long-press if needed.

fixSteps.title: Dry head mount
fixSteps.instruction: Remove head and dry the collar with a towel.

fixSteps.title: Reseat head
fixSteps.instruction: Click new/same head firmly back on.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold mode+power for 15 seconds to clear settings.

whenToCallPro: If red ring persists after reset.

title: Brushing stops briefly during use
fullDescription:
If the brush stops mid-use and restarts, the battery may be old and unable to sustain load, or the pressure sensor is triggering shutdown when pressed hard.

Check session graph in app for pressure spikes and run a full-charge cycle.

fixSteps.title: Ease pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use lighter touch during brushing.

fixSteps.title: Full charge
fixSteps.instruction: Charge until green steady LED.

fixSteps.title: Check runtime
fixSteps.instruction: Under 5 days runtime indicates end-of-life battery.

title: iO color display is black
shortDescription: Display dead — firmware crash or hardware fault.
fullDescription:
The iO 7/9/10 color display should show battery and mode on power. A blank screen can be a firmware crash (fix via long reset) or a display cable fault.

Hold power+mode for 15 seconds until a hard reset animation plays.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold power+mode 15 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Full charge
fixSteps.instruction: Charge overnight in case of BMS lockout.

fixSteps.title: App firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Pair via app and check for firmware update.

whenToCallPro: Blank display after reset and firmware update.

faq.q: Is the brush usable without display?
faq.a: Yes, but mode changes are blind.
